findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update is skipped when the IDP's organization is disabled, leaving hidden or non-public IDPs on the login page
findings.body:
`update()` takes `original` from `getById()` (line 91). That returns the organization-aware wrapper (lines 135-141), whose `isEnabled()` is false whenever the IDP's organization is disabled (lines 436-441). `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates the login predicate on that wrapper (line 405), but the cached ID sets were built from the DB, which ignores organization state.

Sequence:
1. Org O is enabled. IDP X is enabled, in O, BROKER_PUBLIC=true, not hidden. A login search loads a cache set containing X.
2. Disable O. The org update invalidates only organization keys (model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/organization/InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:300-315). `cacheKeyForLogin` is referenced only in this file, so the login caches are not touched.
3. Set X to hideOnLogin=true through the admin REST API. `updated` is a raw model (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/IdentityProviderResource.java:191-197). `original` is false because the org is disabled, and `updated` is false because it is hidden. Both are false, so the method returns at lines 405-407 without invalidating.
4. Re-enable O. `getForLogin(ALL, O)` returns the cached X. Its wrapper `isEnabled()` is now true. The bean's filter checks only `isEnabled()` and `existingIDP` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:79-82). `searchForIdentityProviders` in the base class does not apply `federatedProviderPredicate()` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:237-242), so X is listed on the login page even though it is hidden.

The same sequence with BROKER_PUBLIC=false shows a non-public organization IDP. Either way the wrong list persists until the next login-affecting invalidation.

Fix: evaluate `original` on the raw stored model instead of the wrapper, for example `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())`. The raw model matches what the cached ID sets were computed from.

findings.title: remove() now reads the DB on every call
findings.body: `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` (line 100) runs before the `isInvalid` check. Previously the DB was read only in the invalid branch (line 103), and the valid-cache branch used the cached model (lines 105-108). The new login invalidation needs only the stored login state, so the cached model in the `else` branch (line 107) is sufficient there. Reuse it to avoid the extra query on every remove.

findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", not the IDPs the test creates
findings.body: Both cleanup registrations in the new test call `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (line 381 in the loop, line 425 for idp-alias-20). They never remove the IDPs created here. This is harmless only if the realm is re-imported per method, which I did not confirm. Register the cleanup with the alias the test created instead.

findings.title: Login-cache tests do not cover creating or removing a login-available IDP, or toggling an organization
findings.body: The only create and remove calls in `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 418-428) use IDPs that are not login-available, so they assert only that nothing is invalidated. No step checks that creating a login-available IDP or removing one invalidates the caches. No step disables or re-enables an organization, which is the case where the wrapper's `isEnabled()` changes (see the defect in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405).

findings.title: getLoginPredicate() now also excludes organization IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC in the base federated-login path
findings.body: The added clause changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`, which is also the default `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227, applied at line 213). The base bean is used when the organization feature is off or the realm has organizations disabled (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:482-486). In that case, a user with a federated identity linked to an organization IDP that is not public is now filtered out where it was listed before. The PR body does not mention this. Is that intended?

findings.title: getForLogin Javadoc omits the public-organization condition
findings.body: The Javadoc (lines 151-152) says an IDP "can be used for login if it is enabled, is not a link-only IDP, and is not configured to be hidden on login page". An organization IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC=true meets those conditions but is excluded by ORG_ONLY and ALL (line 180) and now by `getLoginPredicate()` (line 254). Add the public-organization requirement to the Javadoc.

contracts.action: getForLogin cached read path (new Infinispan override, called by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean on every login page render)
contracts.before_after: Before: each call ran the DB query through the default getForLogin. After: the first call per mode and organization caches the ID set; later calls resolve each ID with getById and fall back to the DB if an ID no longer resolves (lines 245-251). The structure matches getByOrganization.
contracts.failure_mode: A stale ID set when a login-affecting change skips invalidation (see the update contract below). A missing ID is handled by invalidating and falling back to the DB.

contracts.action: IDP update() invalidation decision for login caches (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate)
contracts.equivalent_path: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:365-368 (registerIDPInvalidation, which uses only the raw id and alias)
contracts.before_after: The sibling uses only id and alias from the org-aware getById result. The new code evaluates the login predicate on that same org-aware result (line 91 to wrapper at 135-141, isEnabled at 436-441) and compares it with the raw updated model.
contracts.visible_effect: After an organization is re-enabled, a hidden or non-public organization IDP can still appear on the login page until the next login-affecting invalidation.
contracts.failure_mode: Skipped invalidation while the organization is disabled and the update changes login availability (hideOnLogin or BROKER_PUBLIC). Silent: no error or log is produced.

contracts.action: Organization enable/disable (admin update of an org) and its effect on login caches
contracts.before_after: No change in this PR. The org update invalidates only organization keys. The login caches are not invalidated, so org state is applied at read time through the wrapper's isEnabled().
contracts.visible_effect: Login IDP visibility for the organization's IDPs changes when the org is toggled, without any login-cache invalidation.
contracts.failure_mode: This is the premise of the update-invalidation defect above. Re-enabling an organization does not invalidate the login caches.

contracts.action: remove(alias) now reads the stored IDP before the cache check
contracts.equivalent_path: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:101-109 (old code read the DB only in the invalid branch)
contracts.before_after: Before: a valid cache entry avoided any DB read. After: every remove calls idpDelegate.getByAlias, even when the cache entry is valid.
contracts.visible_effect: None on the UI. One extra query per remove.
contracts.failure_mode: None beyond the extra query. storedIdp is null if the alias is absent, and getLoginPredicate handles null.

contracts.action: Bean filter now re-checks isEnabled() for the ORG_ONLY (no org) and ALL branches
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:66-70 (the organization.getIdentityProviders() branch already filters on idp.isEnabled())
contracts.before_after: Before: no isEnabled check on these branches. After: the wrapper's isEnabled() also checks the organization, so IDPs of disabled orgs are removed.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page hides organization IDPs whose organization is disabled.

contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227 (default federatedProviderPredicate, applied at line 213 in the linked-broker path)
contracts.before_after: Before: the predicate checked enabled, link-only and hide-on-login. After: it also excludes organization IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC=true. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate (lines 86-97) combines this with the same public check, so that path is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: On the base bean path (organizations feature off or realm organizations disabled), users whose linked IDP is a non-public organization IDP no longer see it.
contracts.failure_mode: A user cannot pick a previously listed IDP on the base path. Intent not confirmed.
contracts.open_question: Is excluding non-public organization IDPs from the base federated-login path intended when the organizations feature is off or disabled in the realm?

summary: Reviewed the four files in this part. The main finding is a fix-level bug in the login-cache invalidation on IDP update (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405). The "original" model is org-aware, so updates made while the IDP's organization is disabled can skip invalidation, and after the org is re-enabled a hidden or non-public org IDP can still show on the login page. Other findings: an unconditional extra DB read in remove(), test cleanup that targets the literal alias "alias", missing test coverage for create/remove of login IDPs and org toggling, a question on the getLoginPredicate change in the base bean path, and a Javadoc gap. I could not build or run the tests (read-only). I checked the test's expected counts (5, 6, 11 and 5, 6, 11) by hand against its own setup. I did not verify that AbstractKeycloakTest re-imports the realm per method, so the leaked-IDP impact of the cleanup finding is unconfirmed.
